summary.one_liner: Pezzo is an open-source, cloud-native LLMOps platform for observing AI operations, managing prompts, and caching LLM calls.
summary.what_it_does: Pezzo describes itself as a fully cloud-native, open-source LLMOps platform. Per the README, it covers prompt management, observability/monitoring of AI operations, and caching, with clients listed for Node.js, Python, and LangChain. The README says it helps troubleshoot issues, claims savings of up to 90% on costs and latency, and lets teams collaborate on prompts and deliver changes. Its infrastructure relies on PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redis, and Supertokens, which can be started with a provided Docker Compose file. Full documentation (architecture, tutorials, and LLM provider recipes) is hosted externally. The repo is a monorepo with an Nx-based server and a console app.
use_cases: monitor LLM application calls and costs
cache LLM responses to cut latency
how_to_run: npx dotenv-cli -e apps/server/.env -- npx prisma migrate deploy --schema apps/server/prisma/schema.prisma
notable: Full stack can be run locally with Docker Compose, per the documentation
Client libraries for Node.js, Python, and LangChain covering prompt management, observability, and caching
Built on open-source infrastructure: PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redis, Supertokens
GraphQL schema with codegen in watch mode for development
caveats: Development setup requires Node.js 18+, Docker, and several manual steps (migrations, separate server, codegen, and console processes)
Cost and latency savings figure is a marketing claim in the README, not independently verified
Detailed setup and architecture live in external documentation
